pr_title: Better error messages when you don't supply an arg
pr_body:
Closes #75 

**gh pr checkout**

From `requires at least 1 arg(s), only received 0` to `requires a PR number as an argument`

**gh pr view**

From `no open pull requests found for branch “empty-pr-list”` to `no open pull requests found for branch “empty-pr-list”. To open a specific PR use a PR number as an argument`

**gh issue view**
From `requires at least 1 arg(s), only received 0` to `requires an issue number as an argument`
pr_comments: I gave this a go with the custom Error struct idea, let me know what you think.

issue_context.title: Better error messages when you don't supply an arg

  - `gh issue view`

review_comments: I forgot to apply this fix to https://github.com/github/gh-cli/pull/142#discussion_r356210308. So I'm hacking it into this PR.
Since `Visit` only activates on changed flags, maybe the body of the method could simply be `userSetFlags = true`

I still believe that this error case deserves to stay here for other potential callers of this function. I think the `pr` return argument should always be present if there was no error. That makes it easier for callers to do error handling (they only have to compare one return value against nil instead of both)

I've run into this problem a few times in go and am not sure how to handle it. If we pass this as an error we can't tell the difference between no pull request matching and a graphql error. So we can't append extra information to the error because we don't know enough about the error. Have you found any patterns that help with this problem?
I did some digging into this and found https://medium.com/@sebdah/go-best-practices-error-handling-2d15e1f0c5ee. So I'm going to try and use that.
Nit: we usually always say `pull request` in docs instead of shortening it to "PR". Do we want to keep this consistent?
We can probably use an error like this in situations where no issue or pr is found, like `gh pr view 239874987`. But I left that for another PR.
